summary: Master monetary policy negotiation and conflict resolution. Learn to build MPC consensus, manage forward guidance, and protect central bank independence.
lede: Monetary policy negotiation helps analysts, advisers, and committee members reconcile economic evidence and competing priorities. The course covers applying the Taylor Rule and Delphi Method, building consensus in committee discussions, and communicating policy decisions through forward guidance.
audienceIntro: This program is designed for mid-to-senior level professionals who operate at the intersection of economic analysis and institutional decision-making.
modules: Economic Modeling as a Negotiation Anchor
Managing Political and External Stakeholder Pressures
Data-Driven Decision Making and AI Integration
Crisis Negotiation and Emergency Liquidity Measures
Synthesis: Building the Policy Consensus Roadmap
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of macroeconomics and at least 3 years of experience in a policy-related, economic research, or financial regulatory role. Familiarity with basic statistical software and central banking terminology is recommended.
